- Overestimate prices when sentiment is positive (especially >0.11) — model tends to overshoot in bullish periods.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative (especially < -0.3) — model fails to capture downside risk or mean reversion.
- Lagged price spikes are often overpredicted — model reacts too quickly to recent highs, missing subsequent pullbacks.
- Mean reversion bias: model holds too much upward momentum after 3–5 consecutive price increases.
- Overshoot after sharp spikes: if sentiment turns negative within 3–5 days after a spike, model fails to correct — overestimates peak.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are overly optimistic in early summer (July–August 2024) — model ignores seasonal cooldowns.
- Sentiment-driven bias: when sentiment is >0.15, model adds 2–3% extra to forecast; when < -0.2, subtracts 1–2% — but doesn’t adjust for volatility clustering.
